https://www.budapesttimes.hu/diplomacy/r.text: The Budapest Times Russia vows ‘tough and painful’ response to diplomat expulsions Russia will give a "tough and painful response for the Russophobic lobby in Budapest," Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told MTI on Tuesday. Zakharova was responding to a question from the Hungarian news agency about the announcement by Foreign Minister Anita Orbán that the government had expelled ten Russian diplomats from Hungary. When asked when the Russian response could be expected, the diplomat stated: “you will find out.” She did not elaborate further. “Every expulsion is an unfriendly step. A mass expulsion, as in this case, is a multiply unfriendly step — confrontational in nature. This is an open provocation, to which Russia will naturally respond in an appropriate manner. But behind the Budapest decision, I see only Brussels — the European Union and NATO,” said Konstantin Kosachev, Deputy Speaker of the upper house of the Russian parliament, to the RIA Novosti news agency. In the senator’s view, all signs indicate that “post-Orbán” Hungary had been “required to prove its loyalty to the anti-Russian course of these two blocs, and Hungary did not resist.” “Considerations regarding the hypothetical benefits of the infamous European solidarity outweighed considerations regarding the practical benefits of maintaining normal relations with Russia. But in any case, it will be Hungarian taxpayers who will foot the bill,” Kosachev added. Anita Orbán stated that, according to the assessment of Hungarian authorities, ten staff members of the Russian mission had been engaged in activities in Hungary that are unacceptable for a diplomat under the Vienna Convention. “Hungary wishes to maintain the necessary dialogue, based on mutual respect and adherence to the rules,” the foreign minister said.
